summary:
# NOTES: Project Gutenberg text "Adventures of Bindle" by Herbert Jenkins (Gutenberg #32285)

## FRONT MATTER
- Blurb: sequel to "The Night Club"; Bindle is a furniture remover (Joseph Bindle). Stories: helping Mr. Hearty advertise new shop; Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room turned into soldiers' billets; Mrs. Bindle takes a lodger; Bindle becomes porter at Fulham Square Mansions and lets same flat to two people; discourages Rev. Andrew MacFie's attentions to niece Millie Hearty.
- Characters: gloomy Ginger, Wilkes (coughs constantly), Huggles, Lady Knob-Kerrick, Dick Little, "Guggers" (Captain, Gordons; stammers "gug-gug"), Mr. & Mrs. Hearty, "Millikins" (Millie).
- Other books by author listed (Bindles on the Rocks, Bindle, Night Club, etc.). Dedication "To the Children of the Dead End" with verse.
- Contents: 16 chapters: I Coming of the Lodger; II Downing Street Sensation; III Air-Raid; IV Duplication of Mr. Hearty; V Gathering of the Bands; VI Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap; VII Courting of Rev. Andrew MacFie; VIII Chapel Conversazione; IX Letting of Number Six; X Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson; XI Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck; XII Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino; XIII Return of Charlie Dixon; XIV Mr. Hearty Yields; XV A Billeting Adventure; XVI Millie's Wedding.

## CH I – Coming of the Lodger
- Bindle & Mrs. Bindle (Lizzie) at supper; she's angry. Bindle reads ad in *The Gospel Sentinel*: "CHRISTIAN HOME wanted by a single gentleman, chapel-goer, temperance, quiet, musical..." signed Lonely.
- Bindle's jokes on lodgers; story of Horace Gaze who returned from front and caught wife with lover at back door.
- Mrs. Bindle: lodger is Mr. Josiah Gupperduck, plays accordion; joins chapel (Alton Road Chapel). Bindle groans; Hearty = Mrs. Bindle's sister's husband, prosperous greengrocer. Bindle: "Mr. Wot-a-duck"; "sounds like a patent mackintosh."
- Gupperduck arrives Monday 8pm: small, thin, large round spectacles, three wisps of hair, short brown beard, red nose, bare upper lip; ears stand out. Lecturer for Society for Suppression of Atheism; "sower of the seed"; "in the service of the Lord."
- Bindle from The Yellow Ostrich; "Gupperducks" jokes; mentions Regent's Park meetings.
- Bindle's special constable duty; "Barker" gun; Bindle says "The Barker" is Fulham name for gun.
- Bindle declines to play-in; Gupperduck retires. Mrs. Bindle rages; Bindle says he's "'ot stuff" if they flirt.

## CH II – A Downing Street Sensation
- Bindle hired by Messrs. Empsom & Daley, cartage contractors; foreman; partner Tippitt (pale weedy youth, cigarette on lip). Spotty the stable-hand.
- Rides horse to Merton; drops off at Drag and Hounds; Tippitt ahead.
- Pantechnicon of John Smith & Co., Merton; two ladies in motor (elder sallow with pince-nez; younger driver). Destination: Mr. Llewellyn John, 110 Downing Street, carved-oak dining-room furniture. Two shillings given.
- Bindle learns van holds suffragettes ("Black and White Raiders", white dresses, coloured sashes). Bindle puts holes-perforated roof; fills with lamp-black (bought at oil-shop, Wimbledon) via watering-can and pea-puffer; covers with tarpaulin.
- Key from lady opposite Parliament. Bindle tells inspector; Chief-Inspector Gunny of Scotland Yard later. Women spill out; Tippitt knocked down; whistle; women herded to Whitehall; refused taxis; wander home by Tube/District; Mr. Llewellyn John watches from window.
- Bindle receives Deputy-Commissioner's cigar; "The Feathers" pub.

## CH III – Air-Raid
- Mr. Hearty, Mr. Gupperduck, Mrs. Hearty ("wheezes", breath), Millie at Hearty's; Bindle as special constable. Millie's sweetheart Charlie Dixon at front.
- Air-raid: all hide in Hearty's potato cellar. Bindle drops scales to scare them; Gupperduck loses spectacles and upper false teeth; Mrs. Bindle faints. "All Clear".

## CH IV – Duplication of Mr. Hearty
- Bindle & Mrs. Bindle quarrel; "Look at 'Earty"; apple pudding.
- Dick Little (flat in Chelsea), brother Tom Little, Guggers (Captain, Gordons, Oxford; stammers). Plan to advertise Hearty's third shop in Putney High Street.
- Six duplicate "Mr. Heartys" (alibis) enter shop; Smith (right-hand man) hides in cellar; Billy Nips errand boy. Mrs. Hearty laughs. Hearty tells Bindle to put them out; they leave whistling.

## CH V – Gathering of the Bands
- Donkeys with boards advertising "ALFRED HEARTY, THE NAPOLEON OF GREENGROCERS"; "PINEAPPLE ALF"; camel "I'VE GOT THE HUMP"; vegetables characters; many brass bands (Pull for the Shore, Sailor; Onward Christian Soldiers; Shall We Gather at the River). Inspector; drummers Ted, Striker, Charlie (cornet). Hearty charged with obstruction.

## CH VI – Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap
- Queues; Mrs. Bindle complains. Bindle's account of Regent's Park atheist meeting.
- Gupperduck beaten at Hyde Park Peace meeting for wounded soldiers; supporters with sandy beard (Peter) hid in tree; little man with long beard (Wayskin) fled.
- Bindle gives Gupperduck brandy—he's temperance.

## CH VII – Courting of Rev. Andrew MacFie
- Rev. Andrew MacFie (Scottish, sandy, tall, lanky, gloomy) courts Millie; "Mrs. Beendle" (his mispronunciation of Bindle). Sister Miss MacFie.
- Lady Knob-Kerrick (Barton Bridge) brought MacFie to Alton Road Chapel; Temperance Fete fiasco (alcohol in lemonade, Bindle responsible; "lemon-and-a-mac").
- MacFie calls on Mrs. Bindle; Bindle interrupts ("Caught you"). Bindle confronts Hearty.
- Bindle's Bible question about David & Uriah, Bathsheba (named "Urrier" and "Millikins").
- Millie: "I should have killed David."

## CH VIII – Chapel Conversazione
- Mr. Sopley retiring; illuminated address, £50 purse, silver hot-water bottle. Glee-party sings "The Glad Eye". Guests: Mr. Pain & Mrs. Pain, Mr. & Mrs. Withers, Mr. Tuddenham & Mr. Muskett, Miss Torkington, Mr. & Mrs. Gash, Mr. Hippitt ("Pip-Pip"), Mrs. Muspratt ("Miss Musk-Rat"). Alice the maid.
- Bindle: "So shall ye all likewise perish" joke; Miss Torkington offended.
- Lady Knob-Kerrick, Miss Strint (companion), John (footman).
- Woman (Calves = John's nickname) claims to be MacFie's secret wife ("Ruthie"/Cissie?—"Nancy" Dane, Dick Little's disguise, Private "Nancy" Dane of Passchendaele Pierrots). Bindle's plan: fake wife; John blows police whistle; panic; "Calves" blames.
- Dane acts as woman; Bindle: "Took 'er name they did" (Calves). MacFie ruined; advertises £20 reward.

## CH IX – Letting of Number Six
- Mrs. Bindle: "air-raid" fear. Bindle temporarily leaves Harridge's Stores to be caretaker at Fulham Square Mansions for Charlie Hart (holiday; Mrs. Hart ill). Mrs. Sedge (Mrs. Hart's mother; drinks "Royal Richard" gin; Kilburn Cemetery = pub).
- Number Seven: choleric ex-Indian civil servant. "Queenie" (maid, Number Eight). Number Twelve (lost Fluffles, Pekinese). Number Eleven (old lady).
- Mr. Jabez Stiffson rents Number Six (3½ gns/week); canary Oscar; wife away; Miss Cissie Boye (actress, revue "Kiss Me Quick" at Regent Theatre) moves in midnight.

## CH X – Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson
- Mr. Stiffson in Cissie's bath; Cissie sees; Bindle's breakfast; clock turned back. Mrs. Stiffson arrives; porridge bowl on Stiffson's head (Mrs. Sedge brings porridge). Mrs. Stiffson trapped in lift; Stiffson flees.

## CH XI – Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck
- Bindle & Ginger, Wilkes, Huggles at The Yellow Ostrich; Ruddy Bill & Scarlet Horse. Gupperduck beaten at Hyde Park/Putney Heath peace meeting; Bindle blames him. Gupperduck to be "camouflaged" (Bindle threatens) and sent away.

## CH XII – Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino
- Scratcher (lantern-jawed, fishy eyes) gets Bindle job as waiter at Napolini's (Regent Street). Italian waiter Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino ("Kayser"; "Okey-Pokey"). Herr Smith (chief superintendent, formerly Herr Siegesmann). Curried prawns; champagne in hot water; Tolmenicino arrested as spy (Defence of the Realm Act); Bindle sacked.

## CH XIII – Return of Charlie Dixon
- Charlie Dixon (Sergeant, 110th Service Battalion, London Regiment) returns on leave (10 days). Dinner at Universal Cafe (3s6d dinner, wine "Number 68", champagne). Charlie proposes; Bindle persuades Millie to marry next Tuesday. Millie drinks champagne first time.

## CH XIV – Mr. Hearty Yields
- Hearty refuses; Bindle bluffs (Mrs. Hearty? "Ole Six-an'-Eightpence"); Hearty crumbles and agrees to wedding ("Toosday").

## CH XV – A Billeting Adventure
- Harridge's pantechnicon with Ginger, Huggles, Wilkes. Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room (The Poplars, Putney Hill) turned into billets for 16 soldiers. Butler Mr. Wilton; housekeeper Mrs. Marlings; footman John/"Calves". Ginger's herring. Lady Knob-Kerrick: "Halt!" Soldiers depart singing "Here we are again". Lady K: "various veins" jibe at Bindle.

## CH XVI – Millie's Wedding
- Wedding at Alton Road Chapel; Bindle wears crush-hat, white rose, canary gloves. Mr. Hearty's hat under carriage. Rev. Sopley marries them. Charlie's parents: Mrs. Dixon (gentle, white hair), Mr. John Dixon (red-faced, loud, "Beer!"). Bindle's "Lost Moses… fifth"; "Marriages are made in Fulham". Bindle: "You can't return your missus." Mrs. Dixon: "You must be a very good man." Newlyweds leave by taxi.

## END
- Gutenberg license text.
